# `Q-1-13` — Array Length Constraint Violation

> An array has too few or too many items for the schema's length
> constraint.

## What this means

A schema can require that an array contain at least *N* items, at
most *M* items, or both. This error fires when your array is
outside that allowed range.

The terminal message names the actual length and the bound that
was violated — either "less than minimum N" or "greater than
maximum M". Inspect both numbers when diagnosing.

## Why this happens

Two typical situations:

- **An empty array where the schema requires at least one item.**
  Defining a configuration block (such as `navbar.left`) but
  leaving its contents list empty.
- **An over-long array.** Less common; usually appears when a
  schema is being strict about a slot intended to hold one or two
  entries.

## How to fix

If the bound is a minimum, add the missing items. The schema
description for the property should explain what each item
represents.

If the bound is a maximum, remove items, or check whether the
content belongs in this property at all — sometimes a long array
is a signal that the configuration is in the wrong shape (for
example, a flat list that wants to be nested into sub-groups).

## Related

- [`Q-1-19`](Q-1-19.qmd) — array uniqueness: the items are unique within the
  array but the array length itself was wrong.
- [`Q-1-16`](Q-1-16.qmd) — object property count: the same constraint, but for
  the number of *keys* in an object rather than the number of
  *items* in an array.
